TraderDesk Paper Venue — Lot Schedule and Order-Size Bands

Reference document TRDS-PAPER-LS-14  |  Revision effective this session  |  Applies to simulated execution only

This document describes how orders are selected, sized and routed on the TraderDesk paper venue. It describes venue mechanics only; it does not set client limits. Client limits live in the account mandate record and take precedence over anything below.

1. Round-lot schedule, current session

A round lot is the venue's standard order quantity for a symbol. Where an order's quantity is not an exact multiple of the round lot, the order is still accepted, but it is routed to the odd-lot queue rather than the continuous book.

SymbolRound lotRouting of sub-lot quantityTypical fill quality vs. round lot
AAPL60 sharesOdd-lot queue (separate book, no opening-auction participation)30–60 bps worse; frequently misses the open
MSFT40 sharesOdd-lot queue20–50 bps worse

The AAPL round lot was raised from 50 to 60 shares for the current session to align ticket sizes with the index-rebalance print. Round lots are reviewed each session.

2. What this means in practice

An AAPL buy of 44 shares is an odd lot on this venue. It will be accepted and will fill, but it prints on the odd-lot book: it does not participate in the opening cross, and the desk's own fill study for the last four sessions shows an average shortfall of 47 bps against the round-lot print on the same side.

A single round-lot ticket is the normal way to enter an AAPL position here. Submitting 60 shares with a limit at the touch produces one clean print at the opening cross.

3. Venue size bands (informational)

BandNotionalHandling
Odd-lotany quantity below the round lotOdd-lot queue; no auction participation
Round lot1× round lotOpening cross eligible; standard routing
Multi-lot2× round lot and aboveSplit across venues to minimize market impact

4. Worked example (AAPL)

Assume a live quote of about $223. One AAPL round lot is 60 shares, i.e. roughly $13,400 notional. That is the venue's standard single-ticket entry size. Whether such a ticket is permitted is a matter for the account mandate, not for this document.

5. Notes

  • Lot sizes
